topic: Biotic and Abiotic Factors in Ecosystems
key_concepts: Biotic factors are the living things in an ecosystem.
Abiotic factors are the non-living things in an ecosystem.
Animals and plants are examples of biotic factors.
Light, water, temperature, soil type, and air are examples of abiotic factors.
Living organisms depend on abiotic factors such as sunlight and water.
Living organisms can influence abiotic factors through their activities.
Changes in one ecosystem component can affect the entire system.
Biotic factors help shape ecosystems and maintain biodiversity.
Abiotic factors shape ecosystems and support life.
Ecosystems contain interconnected biotic and abiotic components.
